questions.question: How should the script authenticate with Gmail?

options.label: OAuth 2.0 browser flow (Recommended)
options.description: Uses a credentials.json from Google Cloud Console; opens a browser on first run to authorize, then stores a token locally for reuse.

options.label: Service account key
options.description: Uses a downloaded service account JSON key — better for automation/servers, but requires domain-wide delegation for personal Gmail.

questions.question: What should the script output for each matching email?

options.label: Human-readable summary (Recommended)
options.description: Print sender, date, subject, and attachment filenames to stdout.

options.label: JSON
options.description: Output a JSON array of objects — easier to pipe into other tools or scripts.

questions.question: How should the script authenticate with Gmail?

options.label: Gmail API + OAuth2 (Recommended)
options.description: Uses Google's official Gmail API with OAuth2. Requires a one-time setup of credentials in Google Cloud Console, but is the most robust and secure approach.

options.label: IMAP + app password
options.description: Connects via standard IMAP protocol using a Gmail app password. Simpler setup but requires enabling IMAP in Gmail settings and generating an app password.

options.description: Save the actual attachment files to a local directory in addition to printing metadata.

questions.question: How should the script authenticate with Gmail?

options.label: OAuth2 (Recommended)
options.description: Standard user OAuth2 flow via google-auth-oauthlib. Requires a credentials.json from Google Cloud Console; user approves access in browser on first run, then a token is cached locally.

options.label: Gmail MCP tools
options.description: Use the Gmail MCP tools already wired into this Claude Code session — no separate credentials needed, but the script would only work inside Claude Code, not as a standalone tool.

options.label: App password / IMAP
options.description: Connect via IMAP with a Gmail app password. Simpler setup but limited search capabilities compared to the Gmail API.

questions.question: What should the script do with the matching emails' attachments?

options.label: List metadata only (Recommended)
options.description: Print email subject, sender, date, and attachment filenames/sizes. No files are downloaded.

options.label: Download attachments
options.description: Save the attachments from the 3 matched emails to a local directory.

options.label: Both
options.description: Print metadata and also download the attachment files.

questions.question: How should the query be provided to the script?

options.label: CLI argument (Recommended)
options.description: Pass the search query as a command-line argument: python search_gmail.py "from:boss subject:report"

options.label: Interactive prompt
options.description: The script prompts the user to type the query when run.
